name: MLX-LM
notable_features: mlx-lm is the LLM package on top of Apple's MLX array framework; Apple Silicon is the only target
Rotating fixed-size KV cache (--max-kv-size) to cap memory at some quality cost
Prompt caching to disk and in memory, reusable as a prefix across turns
Configurable prefill step size (--prefill-step-size, default 2048) to trade peak memory against prompt speed
Batched generation (batch_generate_response, BatchGenerator) plus a threaded OpenAI-compatible server with separate decode and prompt concurrency knobs
First-party quantization pipeline that converts and uploads models to the mlx-community HF org
Distributed inference and fine-tuning via mx.distributed, with a --pipeline switch for pipeline rather than tensor parallelism
hardware_caveats: Apple Silicon and macOS only - MLX has no CUDA, ROCm, Linux-CPU or Windows path. This is a hard boundary, not a preference
mlx_lm.server exposes batching, but --kv-bits (4 or 8 bit KV cache quantization) explicitly disables batching and serves one request at a time, so enabling KV quantization costs you concurrency

Models much larger than system RAM are slow unless macOS 15+ wired-memory behaviour is in play; the limit is raised with sysctl iogpu.wired_limit_mb, and without it you get a [WARNING] that the model will likely be slow
Adapters (LoRA) and draft models cannot be combined with distributed mode - the loader raises on that combination
Distributed mode also loses adapter support entirely, and the prompt cache and quantized-KV paths are separate features from batching
Large-model speed relies on MLX wiring model and cache memory outside the normal allocator, which needs macOS 15 or newer
best_for: Local Mac development and personal use, where Metal is fast and battery/thermals matter
Quantized models from mlx-community that were converted specifically for MLX, since those are the tuned path
Fine-tuning or LoRA work on Apple Silicon, which mlx-lm supports natively including on quantized models
avoid_for: Any shared or multi-tenant server - you want vLLM-Metal (see [[vllm-metal]]) if you need paged KV and real continuous batching on a Mac
Workloads needing KV-cache quantization and request concurrency at the same time
notes: 'prefix-cache' here is mlx-lm's prompt cache (an LRU of saved prompt KV plus explicit prompt-cache files), not a radix tree and not vLLM's block-level automatic prefix caching. mlx-lm's own quantized formats (4-bit, 8-bit, and bf16) are distinct from GGUF and from AWQ/GPTQ; safetensors is the on-disk container.
